claude.performance_metric: cumulative full cost ceiling charges ~$947.1mm through 12/31/2020; FY2019 net loss $449.305mm
claude.rationale: p5 is coded 1 because the slice documents a realized fracture at the process/organization interface: repeated senior-leadership turnover (CEO/CFO separations Feb 2018, a CEO transition Dec 2019, CFO/COO separations July 2020), a 2018 proxy contest with Icahn that replaced a majority of the board, and multiple workforce reductions (Q1 2018, Q2 2019) — sustained conflict between the operating organization and its people/management over the window. p4 is uncertain because the impairment/ceiling charges reflect commodity/asset-value dynamics, and the slice provides no documented evidence of the acquired product misaligning with operating processes specifically. The slice does not describe the controlling-intent archetype (t1) or the reconciliation of two business models (t2), so both are uncertain; no product/process incoherence is otherwise documented.

grok.performance_metric: cumulative $947.1M full-cost ceiling charges through FY2020
grok.rationale: The slice documents progressive net losses and $947.1M cumulative full-cost ceiling impairments on the oil-and-gas asset base, plus North Park Basin divestiture and leadership/board turnover, but contains no evidence that an acquired product line failed to align with operating processes over time, so p4_pathway is 0. Repeated CEO/CFO/COO separations, the 2018 Icahn proxy contest, and workforce reductions are recorded, yet none are framed as operations-integration fracture against organization/culture, so p5_pathway is 0.

openai.performance_metric: $947.1 million cumulative full cost ceiling charges through December 31, 2020
